temporaryHarness.defenderFinding: Owner inspection of Get-MpThreatDetection recorded Trojan:Win32/PowhidSubExec.B with successful remediation. The affected resource was the large inline PowerShell acceptance command; no Ananke, Horae, Moirae, or Node executable/file was identified as the detected resource.

harnessFindings.quotingDefect: The first process-launch attempt passed the Ananke script path D:\Users\fleur\Project Ananke\packages\runtime-core\dist\server.js as an unquoted Start-Process -ArgumentList element. Windows PowerShell split the path at spaces, so Node received D:\Users\fleur\Project and reported that truncated path as the module to load. The analogous Moirae path also contained spaces. This was a defect in the acceptance harness.
harnessFindings.nodeDriverEndpointDefect: The first Node driver supplied Horae an Ananke base URL ending in /api even though the established Horae inspection binding appends /api itself. Horae therefore queried the non-canonical /api/api inspection path and returned unavailable before dispatch. The driver has been corrected to pass the transport base; no second live run was performed.
harnessFindings.independenceBasis: The quoting defect occurred on the first attempted child-process launch. Defender separately blocked/remediated the large inline PowerShell harness according to the owner-inspected Defender event. Neither event is being used as evidence of a Fates runtime failure, and the Defender event is not being classified as a confirmed false positive.

whyPowerShellWasUsed: The existing Windows owner-local Slice 02 acceptance pattern used PowerShell Start-Process, hidden child processes, redirected logs, readiness polling, and cleanup. That precedent explains the choice, but the large inline generated command introduced quoting and reviewability risk and is not the proposed 003A replacement.
